title: Finite bidirectional factor/recompose kernel
description: Turn kerf into an accretive finite behavioral-factorization engine. The active spine first checks a supplied context-relative boundary map, then checks exact synchronous recomposition, then binds the loop to one real kerf revision. Semantic certificates, bounded factor search, exact morphisms, and migration validation accrete only after that real loop exists. Deferred contracts, model learning, and generic wiring retain their design content but do not block the first theorem.
acceptance_criteria: At one fixed kerf revision, a finite repository-bound observation fixture passes through an additive loop consisting of a checked supplied factor map, a finite factor representation, and exact synchronous recomposition checked against the protected reference behavior. Nearby illegal factor maps and recompositions are rejected with deterministic semantic witnesses. Existing commands retain their stdout, stderr, exit-code, and schema behavior. Exactness is claimed only for supplied finite models, contexts, maps, factors, and bounds. No child claims universal program equivalence or a scalar architecture energy.
close_reason: Reclosed after child bf-engine-mat.7 was repaired and independently reverified at clean exact revision 1362403b3a707f30f0cc3c9f9ce74140947cdb60. The finite factor/recompose/self-host spine remains green and the migration validator now preserves nested input-error taxonomy across the entire supplied graph. The two deferred successor ideas remain explicitly unimplemented and nonblocking under this epic description; --force is used only because Beads retains those deferred parent-child records. Exact root gates: 97 lib + 26 CLI + 5 self-host, strict Clippy/fmt/JSM/diff, UBS 0 critical, clean self-host 8/8. Independent migration taxonomy audit passed 19/19 direct and precedence probes; Fable review found no blocker.

title: Check supplied context-relative factor maps
description: Add the namesake theorem checker. The input supplies a finite deterministic machine, an optional output-blind context monitor, and q mapping every reachable machine-state by context-state pair to a boundary-state ID. Retain the context as external side information and check that protected observation, enabled-action emission, and successor q-state factor through q wherever the context enables the action. Success emits the induced finite boundary representation with constrained and explicitly unconstrained transitions. Ownership: new factor module, one CLI operation, examples, and focused tests. Evidence: focused unit and CLI tests plus all repository gates at the exact revision.
acceptance_criteria: A strict versioned schema supplies exactly every reachable machine-state by context-state pair, rejects duplicate, missing, unreachable, unknown, or empty mappings, and validates only the declared positive product-state bound. Observation must be constant on each q-fibre; when two fibre members both enable an action, emission and successor q-state must agree; different enabled-action domains remain legal because context is retained externally. Success emits canonical initial state, observation, and per-action constrained or unconstrained transitions. Failure returns a deterministic minimum pair of shortest access traces and the offending action where applicable. Tests cover context-side-information positive, observation conflict, emission conflict, successor conflict, missing and extraneous entries, unreachable source states, declaration-order invariance, zero bound, and bound exhaustion returning unknown. Nonclaims exclude minimality, larger contexts, source-code equivalence, liveness, timing, and unmodeled effects. Existing command outputs remain behavior-identical.
close_reason: Delivered context-retained factor-map checking at parent HEAD c8a0e0b9e2e196823dd05094084395ede8a2791f; settled factor.rs SHA-256 ca44bcaaa03cd162d88d938482e077259f7a5d9269ad82b6d733241cf2e8ca99. Exact map validation, three factor laws, induced partial representation, shortlex minimum witnesses, structural-error precedence, and truthful unknown handling are covered by 30 unit and 11 CLI tests. cargo fmt, all-target tests, strict Clippy, jsm validation, git diff check, and UBS exit 0 passed; all six legacy result SHA-256 values remained byte-identical. Oracle found two contract defects and one witness claim defect, all fixed with discriminating regressions; independent Fable and finite all-pairs audits found no remaining theorem counterexample.

title: Check exact finite machine morphisms and sections
description: Check one supplied total state function between finite deterministic machines with a shared action alphabet. The base claim is either an all-state pointed coalgebra morphism or the lifted map f×id_context on the reachable source/context product. Initial, observation, emission, and transition-commutation laws remain distinct. Optional global carrier-surjectivity and exact all-state isomorphism are claims about f. A supplied total section g is checked separately for right-inverse, reverse-morphism, and two-sided-inverse claims. No relational simulation, partial maps, action renaming, approximation, lens language, or map inference exists in v1.
acceptance_criteria: A strict kerf.morphism.v1 schema contains exactly one total supplied f map and rejects duplicate, missing, empty, or unknown entries and duplicate claims. Reachable-scope failures carry the shortest canonical exposing word; all-state failures use a canonical state/action coordinate and never fabricate a trace for an unreachable state. Global carrier-surjectivity reports the least uncovered target. A supplied total g is checked pointwise for f(g(t))=t; g-as-morphism and g(f(s))=s are separate explicit results. Exact machine isomorphism is accepted only under all-state scope and requires an all-state morphism plus global injectivity and surjectivity. Unreachable states never strengthen a reachable-only theorem. Each requested reachable traversal has a positive explicit product bound; exhaustion is unknown. Semantic failure is a successful analysis, no source map is inferred, declaration order cannot change the result, and existing command bytes remain unchanged.

All-state and reachable-under-context laws, canonical witnesses, global carrier/isomorphism claims, supplied section claims, per-direction unknown bounds, and strict map/claim validation are covered by 87 library, 23 CLI, and 5 self-host tests; strict Clippy, JSM validation, diff check, and changed-source UBS triage passed. Exact clean self-host matched 8/8 existing command cases with executable 13aa1dfe09bae22e3364aa09d5815da6706b326612d449bd36c37e0c5bd41b2b. Fable's adversarial review was green after identifying and verifying removal of an eager word-construction asymptotic trap. An independent finite oracle made 15,698 CLI calls across exhaustive small maps, two seeded random families, bounds, inverses, and declaration permutations with zero mismatches.

title: Verify finite semantic equivalence certificates
description: Add small proof objects only after the real self-host loop identifies their consumer. Positive equivalence uses an explicit reachable relation closed under the supplied context. Inequivalence replays witness words. Factor-map and arithmetic receipts use their native locally checkable laws. Provenance records input, bounds, version, and optional revision identity separately from semantic validity; re-running the producing algorithm or matching a Git build is not proof.
acceptance_criteria: A versioned positive equivalence certificate contains the initial left-right-context tuple and is checked locally for equal observations, equal enabled emissions, and successor closure. Witness replay deterministically validates negative results and also checks a recorded trace against a supplied model. Changed inputs, missing closure tuples, altered observations or emissions, invalid successors, and tampered witnesses are rejected. Certificate validity does not depend on the producing kerf revision; provenance mismatch is a separate typed result. No signature, source-equivalence, or context-assisted minimality claim is made.
close_reason: Delivered at 0c96d8b77ec7373cea466a633c449de216926a08: verify-certificate locally checks canonical hash-bound reachable cross-machine relations, inequivalence witnesses, and recorded traces; provenance is typed and orthogonal. Factor/arithmetic laws require no separate certificate kind in v1. Exact gates: 54 unit, 17 CLI, 5 self-host tests; strict Clippy; JSM; staged UBS 0 critical. Clean self-host matched 8/8 with executable feb8282a8033ab0cd8b8a82b959f60cf33af8d7d546025bb5ffdf05de91bc81a. Independent Fable audit green; chain doubling 1200 to 2400 was linear 0.045s to 0.091s at about 16 MiB after parent-pointer fix. Oracle semantic audit green; its I/O and canonical-hash findings were fixed and regression-tested.

title: Check exact synchronous recomposition
description: Check the inverse finite direction after a lawful factor representation exists. Accept named total deterministic factors over one identical external action alphabet, explicit observation and action-indexed emission readouts, a reference machine, the same optional context, and finite bounds. Construct only the reachable synchronous product and compare its protected behavior with the reference using kerf shortest-witness semantics. Generic typed ports, hidden actions, feedback, delay, hierarchy, and asynchrony remain future model-class extensions.
acceptance_criteria: A strict kerf.recompose.v1 schema accepts one or more named kerf.factor-representation.v2 values, each carrying an explicit certified output-blind context, plus a shared identical external action alphabet, finite table readouts over factor observations and action-indexed emissions, a total deterministic reference machine, a proposed output-blind context, and positive product, pair, and witness bounds. Semantic JSON maps reject duplicate raw object members. Only reachable synchronous products of factor state, per-factor certified-context state, and proposed-context state are explored in canonical factor-ID and action order. Missing or duplicate proved-reachable readouts, detached v1 representations, and invalid references are invalid input. A proposed-context action disabled by any factor certified context or using any unconstrained factor coordinate creates a shortest canonical unproved word including the offending action; it is never completed implicitly. Definite inequivalence dominates holes and resource frontiers: the shortest proved mismatch and shortest exposed hole are both reported, with witness minimality marked completion_robust or proved_region_only. Otherwise the verdict is equivalent or unproved. Product, pair, or witness exhaustion returns unknown only when no fully exposed mismatch already decides inequivalence. Tests cover direct one-factor consumption of bf-engine-mat.1, widened-context holes including the all-coordinates-constrained stepwise-existential counterexample, a genuine two-factor positive with unreachable Cartesian tuples, shorter-sibling inequivalence, an earlier hole plus later proved mismatch, pair- and product-bound sibling precedence, initial mismatch before product exhaustion, invalid and duplicate readouts, raw duplicate JSON members, invalid references and v1 artifacts, declaration-order invariance, zero bounds, and all three bound classes. The factor producer deliberately upgrades only its lawful representation to v2 plus canonical certified_context; unlawful factor output and every other existing command remain byte-behavior-identical. Nonclaims exclude producer provenance, typed ports, hidden actions, feedback, delay, hierarchy, asynchrony, readout inference, factor inference, and source-code equivalence.

The checker preserves certified context, reports every exposed hole without completion, returns fully exposed mismatches before resource frontiers with honest minimality scope, and rejects duplicate semantic JSON members. 46 unit and 14 CLI tests, fmt, strict Clippy, jsm validation, git diff check, and final staged UBS exit 0 passed. Seven legacy output hashes remained byte-identical. Oracle defects were fixed with discriminating regressions; Fable reran the exact reproducers and 700 independent differential finite models with zero remaining discrepancy.

title: Finite safety contracts for a named replacement case
description: Deferred extension. Reactivate only when a named replacement case cannot be discharged by exact factorization, recomposition, or whole-model comparison. The eventual v1 is finite safety with explicit environment and component action polarity, exact compatibility, implementation direction, and assumption discharge; no generic liveness or contract algebra.
acceptance_criteria: Activation requires an executable named consumer. Finite safety assumptions and guarantees distinguish environment inputs and component outputs; circular assumptions cannot establish themselves; one legal independent replacement passes and an incompatible or circular replacement fails. Progress, fairness, liveness, and substitutivity beyond the encoded finite safety property are nonclaims.
notes: Deferred from the active spine: no independent-substitution consumer exists. Reactivate after the thin self-host exposes a concrete whole-model limitation.

title: Bounded model acquisition for a named teacher
description: Deferred extension. Reactivate with one named real teacher adapter after hand-authoring a finite model becomes the measured bottleneck. Queries, states, revision, workload identity, counterexamples, and budgets must be recorded. Passive traces remain evidence, never equivalence.
acceptance_criteria: Activation starts with a named real teacher adapter and an existing exact checker that consumes its output. A deterministic finite reference teacher can produce an equivalent learned machine in the supported setting; contradictory answers are errors; exhausted query or state budgets return unknown; every split links to its counterexample or query. Approximate conformance teachers and passive traces never emit exact equivalence.
notes: Deferred from the active spine: the first self-host model is small and authored; no teacher endpoint or measured acquisition bottleneck exists.

title: Validate proof-carrying migration graphs
description: Validate a supplied finite graph of complete modeled states and directionally proof-carrying transformation edges. Every node gives the complete state of one fixed carrier universe: one finite machine and one writer per carrier, plus at most one named positive-rank cleanup obligation. Every edge changes exactly one modeled carrier, embeds and locally re-verifies a source-to-target compare-equivalence certificate under that carrier’s graph-fixed context, binds exact authority transfer and cleanup-transition claims to endpoint state, and may separately claim a reverse evidence bundle. Revision and operation strings are labels, not execution proof. V1 validates the supplied graph; it does not optimize paths, infer models, or aggregate unlike costs.
acceptance_criteria: A strict kerf.migration-graph.v1 schema rejects duplicate, empty, missing, or unknown IDs; invalid machines or contexts; differing carrier universes; zero cleanup ranks; malformed endpoint references; and malformed nested certificate schemas or subjects before producing a graph verdict. Canonical carrier encodings, not JSON order or asserted hashes, determine endpoint equality. Every edge has exactly one changed carrier and names it; no machine or writer outside that carrier may change. Its embedded compare-equivalence certificate is structurally valid, reverified, accepted, and directionally bound to the source and target carrier machines under one graph-fixed carrier context. The affected-carrier writer delta and declared authority transfer match exactly, with one writer per carrier at every node. Optional reverse evidence embeds independently accepted reverse-bound evidence and exact reversed authority transfer; its non-empty operation is metadata, not an executable rollback or graph edge. Cleanup state belongs to nodes. Each edge claim exactly matches one of debt-free-to-debt-free, introduction to one positive-rank obligation, strict same-obligation rank decrease, or discharge to debt-free. Every positive-debt node has an outgoing edge; therefore every maximal continuation discharges within its starting rank, wholly positive cycles and obligation swaps are impossible, and debt-free-to-positive-to-debt-free cycles remain legal. Structural defects, including malformed nested certificate inputs, are typed input errors; otherwise the result reports the canonical first invalid edge or positive sink independent of declaration order. No multi-carrier edge, carrier creation/removal, partial proof, path search, Pareto optimization, scalar debt energy, source equivalence, cross-carrier composition, Git binding, operation execution, rollback availability, or runtime authority enforcement is claimed.
close_reason: Reclosed after correcting the post-push Oracle taxonomy defect at exact clean revision 1362403b3a707f30f0cc3c9f9ce74140947cdb60. Migration preparation now structurally verifies and caches every forward/reverse embedded certificate before any completed graph verdict, so malformed same-edge, later-edge, or reverse evidence cannot be masked; well-formed false/stale evidence still returns exit 0 valid:false. Root reran 97 lib + 26 CLI + 5 self-host tests, strict Clippy/fmt/JSM/diff checks, and UBS with 0 critical. Clean self-host matched 8/8 with executable sha256 1a6c34347691c9c4340b098a79d89ea7298fc4de7d2365065c668bb7b0a3e7f5. Independent finite verifier passed 19/19 direct/masking probes on exact source hashes; Fable independently reproduced the taxonomy, unsupported-kind, reverse, cleanup, and ordering controls with no blocker. Nonclaims remain source equivalence, operation execution, rollback availability, and real-world graph completeness.

title: Enumerate and admit bounded factor maps
description: Search only after a real self-host consumer exists. For one supplied finite machine and context, enumerate q-partitions of canonically ordered reachable product states using a label-symmetry-free finite representation, and admit candidates only through the factor-map laws. This is exact bounded ground truth, not a generator zoo.
acceptance_criteria: Inputs declare maximum boundary states plus product-state and candidate-enumeration bounds. Enumeration uses canonical restricted-growth or equivalent symmetry-free labels, reports exact counts per completed cardinality, and emits a deterministic coverage summary. Reaching a candidate bound before a cardinality is complete returns unknown and emits no minimum claim. A minimum k may be claimed only after every smaller represented partition was completely rejected and at least one size-k partition passed. CP-SAT, MILP, LLM proposals, equality saturation, annealing, graph partitioning, heuristic incumbents, Pareto robustness, and metric unification are outside v1. If a later coordinate consumes transport output, exact rationals must flow without rounding or format loss.
close_reason: Delivered at d775fe37cb80ddf1a88cb3eb8d0568899130fcf7: exact restricted-growth factor search found the self-host model minimum k=2 with canonical map 0001; candidate and product exhaustion remain unknown. Clean revision proof matched all 8 raw process cases with executable sha256 79630bb4feec991772ed220d032688de5c1f0a80b4ce7b33c1c8b4e0e066e320 and corpus sha256 a0833db5429c7a830db9089e63c5b498b40a600442cbcfbb8abd3cc9a6e909c8. Final gates: 64 unit, 19 CLI, 5 self-host, strict Clippy, fmt, JSM, diff-check, changed-source UBS with 0 critical, Fable differential fuzz and exact-k n<=9 review green.

title: Bind one thin kerf self-host adapter
description: Expose the finite factor/recompose spine to reality early. Bind one exact kerf revision and a fixed executable corpus to explicit protected process observations, author the smallest finite model justified by that corpus and source-grounded assumptions, check a nontrivial factor map, and check synchronous recomposition. This adapter is a falsifier and reusable frontend seed, not source inference or a universal Rust analyzer.
acceptance_criteria: At one exact revision, an executable adapter invokes the real kerf binary on a fixed finite corpus whose protected observation names raw exit status, stdout bytes, and stderr bytes or a frozen explicit normalization. The corpus includes a successful LTS operation, a typed error, a resource-limit unknown, and a distinguishing witness. A nontrivial supplied q passes and a nearby illegal q fails semantically; a supplied recomposition passes against the same model and a nearby corruption fails. Existing CLI observations remain unchanged. Discovery, contracts, generic wiring, architecture search, migration optimization, and invented cost metrics are explicit non-goals.

title: Semantic architecture compiler for greenfield and brownfield systems
description: Build one canonical evidence-bearing semantic model that can be authored before code or recovered from a pinned codebase, then compile explicit finite obligations into Kerf and implementation obligations into downstream work without laundering inference into proof.
acceptance_criteria: A versioned companion CLI and skill support greenfield and brownfield models, retain contradictions and unknowns, emit deterministic evidence-bound projections and a cycle-free work graph, integrate with the existing exact Kerf kernel and downstream seam/refactor skills, and document the precise computability and evidence limits.

title: Canonical semantic IR and epistemic claim ledger
description: Define strict versioned entities, typed relations, evidence provenance, claim scopes and verdicts, authority/effect protocols, work declarations, and Kerf projection receipts. Input validity is separate from model completeness.
acceptance_criteria: Strict deterministic parsing rejects duplicate fields, IDs, bad references, malformed hashes, and type-invalid relations. The IR expresses both greenfield and brownfield subjects, proved finite versus bounded support versus hypothesis/assumption/refutation/unknown/stale, explicit conflicts, nonclaims, and complete projection omission receipts.
close_reason: Delivered strict kerf.semantic-model.v1 IR with duplicate/reference/type/cycle checks, separate epistemic and reality axes, content-bound exact receipts, closure classes, greenfield and brownfield subjects, and adversarial tests.

title: Frontier evaluation corpus and durable documentation
description: Maintain adversarial greenfield/brownfield fixtures, cross-domain mechanism classifications, architecture documentation, skill instructions, and self-host coverage for the semantic compiler.
acceptance_criteria: The corpus covers claim laundering, contradictions, ordering, invalid inputs, rare-path omissions, authority/effect controls, declaration order, projection tampering, work cycles, and resource limits. Documentation distinguishes theorem, finite check, inference, heuristic, and metaphor and cites primary sources.

title: Deterministic semantic model analyzer with witnesses
description: Analyze structurally valid semantic models for traceability gaps, claim laundering, contradiction, authority ambiguity, derived-view validity gaps, effect-recovery gaps, and unaccounted projection coordinates.
acceptance_criteria: Every supported finding has stable code, severity, sorted subjects, evidence basis, explanation, and next action. Positive, negative, invalid, declaration-order, provenance, contradiction, and nearby-control tests pass; findings never claim source equivalence.
close_reason: Delivered deterministic typed analyzer with exact structural witnesses, evidence-policy findings, closure and authority checks, cross-subject evidence guards, and source-correspondence laundering blockers; semantic test suite passes.

title: Compile model gaps into a dependency-safe work graph
description: Turn analyzer findings and declared work into a deterministic preview graph suitable for later Beads application, retaining requirement, change, evidence-gate, cleanup, and external-binding traceability.
acceptance_criteria: The compiler emits stable work IDs and exact dependency edges; prerequisite observation/model/evidence obligations precede implementation; conflicts and cycles prevent applyability; it performs no tracker mutation and does not treat tracker status as semantic evidence.
close_reason: Delivered pure deterministic kerf.semantic-work-graph.v1 compiler with ordered generated obligations, declared-work cycle detection, and byte-identical repeated output; it performs no tracker mutation.

title: Project explicit model slices into existing Kerf schemas
description: Compile declared semantic-model slices to current Kerf inputs with exact entity/relation coverage, omissions, assumptions, canonical bytes, hashes, and a source-claim ceiling.
acceptance_criteria: At least one real greenfield and one brownfield projection parse as current Kerf inputs; every scoped entity and incident relation is mapped or explicitly omitted; canonical target bytes and SHA-256 are deterministic; exact output is limited to the supplied finite projection and cannot promote source correspondence.
close_reason: Delivered total map-or-omit projections for all existing Kerf input schemas, resolvable pointer validation, canonical target hashes, manifests, and separate greenfield/implementation example projections accepted by Kerf.

title: Recover a partial semantic model from the Kerf repository
description: Build the first named brownfield adapter from pinned Kerf source, manifests, Git history, and the revision-bound self-host corpus. Preserve blind spots; do not infer a complete LTS from passive evidence.
acceptance_criteria: At a pinned clean revision the adapter emits repeatable structural and observation evidence with source selectors, coverage, omissions, and explicit unknowns. Dirty state, revision drift, generated/configured code, and passive-trace incompleteness are reported rather than normalized away.

title: Greenfield authoring and bounded architecture synthesis
description: Add a constrained authoring grammar for requirements, ports, carriers, observations, contracts, and work. Use counterexample-guided bounded search only after the grammar and protected semantics are declared.
acceptance_criteria: A finite grammar can generate and locally check a satisfying model or report bounded unknown/checked unsatisfiable-within-grammar; contradictory requirements produce witnesses; no universal shortest-program claim is made.

title: Bridge semantic findings to seam and isomorphic refactor skills
description: Export evidence-bound packets for optimize-program-seam-topology, de-monolithization, and isomorphic simplification, and reimport their results as hypotheses or bounded evidence at the correct ceiling.
acceptance_criteria: Fold-graph scores never become semantic proofs; Type-IV clone merges require behavioral evidence; generated and justified monolith controls do not auto-split; exported packets include protected observations, blind spots, proof gates, and retirement conditions.

title: Check local-to-global contract consistency
description: Represent finite overlap contracts and restriction maps, then construct a global assignment or emit a checkable conflict core. Keep this layer distinct from transition behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Finite encoded overlap instances return a checked global section or a locally checkable unsatisfiable core; pairwise agreement alone is not reported as global consistency; consistently wrong local models remain outside the claim.

title: Compile architecture work into proof-carrying migration candidates
description: Use the same bounded rewrite grammar for endpoint proposals and migration operations, projecting compatible one-carrier steps into the current Kerf migration validator.
acceptance_criteria: Every emitted migration edge binds source/target carriers, authority transfer, proof receipt, and cleanup rank; unsupported multi-carrier atomic steps remain explicit; a lower-cost endpoint cannot bypass an unproved intermediate.
